newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta shares end firmer on selective buying.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta shares end firmer on selective buying.

text.p: Jakarta share prices ended firmer despite weak market sentiment on Wednesday on the back of selective buying of a few big-capitalised stocks and certain secondaries, brokers said.
The Jakarta Composite Index rose 1.11 points, or 0.20 percent, to close at 568.86 points after touching an intra-day low of 566.96 points. Gainers led losers by 57 to 48, with 63 counters unchanged.
Brokers said the market was likely to continue being mixed on Thursday as many local investors were trading on a short-term basis.
"But possible selective foreign buying could drive the index into positive territory," said a broker from a Hong Kong-based securities house.

Brokers said overall trading was slow with most buying done by foreigners while local investors were cashing out gains quickly. They said locals were looking to fund applications to next week's initial public offering of Bank Negara Indonesia (BNI) 1946, in which BNI plans to float about 1.1 billion shares at a price of 850 rupiah each.
Cement blue-chip Semen Gresik was one target of foreign buying following its good nine-month results, brokers said.
It rose 75 rupiah to 6,525 rupiah on a volume of 713,000 shares.

Cigarette firm Sampoerna rose 350 rupiah to 21,300 on a volume of 220,500 shares on what brokers ascribed to foreign buying in the wake of its apparently abandoning a move to buy into car-maker Astra International.
State-controlled mining firm Tambang Timah was among the losers on limited foreign selling. It fell 3.85 percent to 3,750 rupiah on a volume of 1.04 million shares.
Fisheries company PT Daya Guna Samudra topped the active list with 5.6 million shares traded, rising 100 rupiah to 2,250.
Brokers said it was in focus following its encouraging debut last week. "Fundamentally, it is a good stock and many investors like it," said one local broker.

Shipping firm Berlian Laju Tanker was actively traded with 1.7 million shares changing hands, rising 50 rupiah to 3,700 rupiah on what brokers said was due to plans for a stock split and to issue bonus shares. The company is to hold a shareholders meeting on Friday to discuss the proposals.
"There is also market talk that the firm will link-up with a partner from Singapore but details are unclear," said one foreign broker.
